newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Drought still looms in Brazil soybean state - coops.
newsitem.headline: Drought still looms in Brazil soybean state - coops.

text.p: No rains were expected in Brazil's key soybean growing regions of Parana and Rio Grande do Sul and the situation in the latter state could become critical if drought continued for the next ten days, agronomists said.

"There is a cold front in Rio Grande do Sul but it is very weak," said Marcio Custodio at independent meteorologists Somar. "The situation in the soybean growing regions of the state remains critical. They have been 15 to 18 days without rain."
But it was too early to predict crop losses, as some cooperatives have started to do, said Midio Antonio Barny of the Rio Grande do Sul agricultural secretariat.
"We can't talk about any drop in the harvest at this stage," Barny said. "But if this drought continues for another 10 days, we could lose 10 to 15 percent of the crop."
Only 30 percent of the crop was in the critical flowering stage, while 30 percent was in the vegetative stage and 40 percent was in the early flowering process.
This meant the soybean could still compensate for the drought if it rained soon, said Barny.
Rainfall in Rio Grande do Sul was only 20 percent of the historical average during the last 20 days.
But the drought affected mainly the south of the state and the corn crop, while the soybean crop concentrated in the north of the state was still relatively unscathed, Barny said.
Custodio at Somar said periods of drought lasting up to two weeks were frequent during the summer season and a stronger cold front was due to hit the south on Jan 17.
He added that conditions in Parana remained normal and soil moisture was good.
